test_title: RRB NTPC CBT 2 (Level-5) Official Paper (Held On: 15 June 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is a Per unit Tax (or Unit Tax)?

options.text: A tax that the factory, imposes on total unit purchase on imports.
A tax that the factory imposes per unit sale of output.
A tax that the government imposes per unit sale of output.
A tax that the government imposes per unit purchase on imports.

solution:
The correct answer is __**A tax that the government imposes per unit sale of output**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A fixed tax **on a product, unrelated to the purchase price, is known as** a per-unit tax.**
 
• It can be shown as a wedge between the supply and demand curves. **PS denotes** the price sellers receive after taxes, while **PB denotes** the amount purchasers pay.
 
• The tax revenue is indicated by the orange rectangle (the per unit tax times the quantity sold).
 
• The producer surplus is coloured in pink, the consumer surplus in blue, and the deadweight loss in purple. [IMAGE: https://demonstrations.wolfram.com/PerUnitTax/] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• A tariff is a charge a nation imposes on imports of goods and services from another nation.
 
• A unit tax is a tax levied by the government on each sale of output, per unit. A unit tax's implementation changes the marginal.
 
• The rising cost curve for the company The supply curve will move to the left as a result.
